title: Train a Vision Transformer from scratch
summary: Implement ViT from numpy + PyTorch on CIFAR-10 then ImageNet-100. Compare against a small CNN baseline. Understand exactly why ViTs need data + scale, and what an MAE-style pretraining schedule buys.
contentIntro:
## What you'll build

Four milestones: a working Vision Transformer trained from scratch + a CNN baseline + an MAE pretraining experiment + an analysis of when each architecture wins.

- ViT-Tiny on CIFAR-10
- CNN baseline (ResNet-18 small) on the same dataset
- MAE pretraining + fine-tune
- Scale-vs-quality analysis on ImageNet-100

By the end you understand why ViTs match CNNs at scale, where they don't, and what self-supervised pretraining buys.

## What you'll build

Four milestones, ~5 weeks. PyTorch + a single GPU (16GB+ recommended). The model is small (~5M params for ViT-Tiny); the experiment is the point, not the scale.

Datasets: CIFAR-10 (60K images, 10 classes) for fast iteration; ImageNet-100 (~130K images, 100 classes) for the scale-vs-quality milestone.

contentGrad:
## What you'll build

A reference ViT implementation + an empirical analysis your team would consult when deciding 'CNN or ViT for our task'. Defense covers: the data scale at which ViTs cross over CNNs, why MAE pretraining helps so much, and the architectural design choices (patch size, position embeddings, MLP ratio) that affect quality.

milestones.title: ViT-Tiny on CIFAR-10
milestones.description:
Implement a Vision Transformer from scratch:

1. **Patch embedding**: Conv2d with kernel = stride = patch_size (try 4×4 and 8×8 for 32×32 CIFAR images).
2. **Position embeddings**: learned 1D, one per patch position.
3. **[CLS] token**: learnable token prepended to the sequence.
4. **Transformer blocks**: standard self-attention + MLP. 6-12 layers; d_model = 192-384; heads = 3-6.
5. **Classification head**: linear layer on the [CLS] token output.

Train on CIFAR-10 (60K images, 50 epochs, AdamW, cosine LR). Measure:
- Top-1 accuracy.
- Wall-clock time.
- Compare patch sizes 4×4 vs 8×8 vs 16×16 (the last gives only 4 patches; expect bad).

In your writeup: a model architecture diagram + training curves + accuracy table by patch size.

criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether the ViT implementation is correct: patch embedding via Conv2d, learned position embeddings, [CLS] token, standard transformer blocks. Common bugs: missing layer norm at the end, wrong attention mask, incorrect [CLS] handling.

Score whether the experiments compare different patch sizes meaningfully and the writeup explains the trade-off (smaller patches → more tokens → quadratic attention cost; larger → fewer tokens → coarser features).
Score the writeup's architecture diagram + training curves.

milestones.title: CNN baseline on the same dataset
milestones.description:
Implement a small ResNet (8-18 layers) and train on the same CIFAR-10 setup. Same training time budget as ViT.

Measure:
- Top-1 accuracy.
- Wall-clock per epoch.
- Final model size (parameters).

In your writeup: side-by-side comparison. Expect CNN to win on CIFAR-10 — small dataset, CNN's inductive bias acts as regularization. ViT typically loses by 2-5%.

This milestone is the 'inductive bias matters at small scale' empirical result. Make it clear in the writeup: at this scale, the CNN wins. We'll see what changes at larger scale in the next milestone.

criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether the ResNet is implemented correctly: residual blocks, batch normalization, standard CNN structure.
Score whether the comparison is fair: same training time, same hyperparameter budget, same data. Is the analysis clear?
Score the writeup's discussion of why CNN wins on small data.

milestones.title: MAE pretraining + fine-tune
milestones.description:
Implement Masked Autoencoder (MAE) pretraining for your ViT-Tiny:

1. **Encoder**: only sees ~25% of patches (75% masked).
2. **Decoder**: lightweight transformer that reconstructs the masked patches' pixel values from the encoder's features + mask tokens.
3. **Loss**: MSE on the masked patches' pixel values.
4. **Pretrain**: 100-200 epochs on CIFAR-10 (or unlabeled images).
5. **Fine-tune**: replace decoder with classification head; fine-tune on labeled CIFAR-10.

Measure:
- Pretrain loss curve.
- Fine-tune accuracy vs from-scratch ViT.

Expected: MAE-pretrained ViT outperforms from-scratch ViT by 3-7%. Sometimes catches the CNN; sometimes not.

In your writeup: pretraining + fine-tuning curves; comparison with from-scratch ViT and CNN baseline.

criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether MAE is implemented correctly: 75% masking, lightweight decoder with mask tokens, MSE on masked patches.
Score whether the experiment shows clear quantitative improvement from MAE pretraining over from-scratch ViT.
Score the writeup's analysis of why MAE pretraining helps.

milestones.title: Scale-vs-quality on ImageNet-100
milestones.description:
Repeat the ViT vs CNN comparison on ImageNet-100 (130K images, 100 classes). Standard 224×224 resolution.

Three configurations:
- ViT-Tiny from scratch.
- ViT-Tiny with MAE pretraining (100 epochs pretrain on the unlabeled subset, then fine-tune).
- ResNet-18 from scratch.

Measure top-1 + top-5 accuracy. Expected ordering: ViT-Tiny + MAE ≈ ResNet-18 > ViT-Tiny from scratch.

Final report:

1. **Comparison table**: rows = (ViT scratch, ViT + MAE, CNN). Columns = CIFAR-10 acc, ImageNet-100 acc, training time.
2. **Discussion**: at what dataset scale does the ViT cross over the CNN? What does MAE pretraining buy at each scale?
3. **Recommendation**: for a hypothetical team training a vision model with 50K images, what would you recommend? What about 5M images? Defend with the data.

This milestone is the synthesis. Show that the inductive-bias-vs-flexibility trade-off is real and visible in your own experiments.

criteria.aiPrompt: Score whether all three configurations are trained correctly with comparable hyperparameters and resources.
Score the cross-over analysis: at what scale does ViT match CNN? Is the analysis defensible?
Score the recommendation: for hypothetical scenarios, does the choice match the empirical evidence?
